correctness.rationale: For full-column-rank real matrices, both polar directions have orthonormal columns and hence identical quadratic-score denominators tr(B). Variational uniqueness proves the upper inequality and commuting equality. The positive-semidefinite polynomial (B−μI)(LI−B) yields the sharp scalar bound vᵀBv/||Bv||≥2√(μL)/(μ+L); nuclear-norm decomposition of GB^-1 and triangle inequality lift it to polar alignment. A 2×2 invertible ε-family gives exactly the limiting squared factor, κ=1 gives equality, and all quantifiers/rank assumptions are explicit. Embedded verify.py independently checks 70 exact rational identities, 2160 random full-rank matrices and true line-search decreases, and five sharpness sequences; computations corroborate but do not prove universal claims.

value.rationale: The motivating algorithm uses polar(G B^-1) and compares its one-step quadratic improvement with polar(G); the source verifies descent but lacks a worst-case score guarantee. The finding establishes an exact condition-number degradation frontier and a commuting/no-loss classification for a natural entire family of strongly convex matrix quadratics. The 2×2 near-rank-one construction shows that anisotropic input curvature alone can destroy a large fraction of the score even under exact line search, while the quantified lower bound forbids worse losses at fixed condition number. This informs when input preconditioning is or is not advantageous without asserting a multi-step or general-curvature conclusion.
